Text:
OPHTHALMIC SURGERY
When indicated, ophthalmology will order antimicrobial prophylaxis before procedures.

# Cataract Surgery

Intracameral moxifloxacin is recommended for use to reduce the risk of post-operative endophthalmitis after cataract surgery only in those patients at highest risk of infection, including the following:

* Patients with prior intravitreal injections
* Immunosuppressed patients
* Patients with significant ocular surface eyelid disease
* Complication occurs during surgery (i.e. capusle rupture, vitreous loss)
* Other possible high risk situations as they arise but not listed above

References:

- Arshinoff S., J Cataract Refract Surg, (2016) 42:1730-1741
Therapy:
## Preferred:

Moxifloxacin 500mcg/0.5ml Eye Inj Intracameral Cataract (Conc.=100mcg/0.1ml)

*Local guidance (Omaha CDSS, Inpatient/Outpatient):*
Polymyxin/trimethoprim ophthalmic drops: 1 drop both eyes four times a day for 2 days prior to surgery, then continue for 2 weeks after surgery.
Ciprofloxacin 0.3 %: 1 drop both eyes four times a day for 2 days prior to surgery then continue for 2 weeks after surgery.
Moxifloxacin 0.5 %: 1 drop both eyes four times a day for 2 days prior to surgery, then continue for 2 weeks after surgery.
Erythromycin 0.5 % ophthalmic ointment: apply thin film to both eyes qid for 2 days prior to surgery, then continue for 2 weeks after surgery.
